rows.speaker: طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة
rows.claim: Reports from Shiite and Sunni channels say the verse was revealed concerning Ali.
rows.anchor: ورد في أسباب النزول من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة أن الآية نزلت في علي

rows.speaker: طرق أهل السنة
rows.claim: Some Sunni reports instead connect the revelation to the emigrants in Abyssinia; other reports give different occasions.
rows.anchor: وفي بعضها ما ورد من طرق أهل السنة أنها نزلت في مهاجري الحبشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the verse wording remains general and links it to the preceding statement that the false gods will become their enemies.
rows.anchor: فعموم لفظ الآية في محله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: At Resurrection, those taken as gods besides God become enemies of their worshippers and disavow both them and their worship.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة أي يكون هؤلاء الذين اتخذوهم آلهة من دون الله ضدا يوم القيامة ويتبرأون منهم ومن عبادتهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The count God makes is the breaths people take, rather than a count of days.
rows.anchor: قال الآباء والأمهات يحصون ذلك ولكنه عدد الأنفاس

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says a person's breaths are steps carrying him toward his appointed death.
rows.anchor: نفس المرء خطاه إلى أجله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali adds that every counted thing diminishes and every expected event arrives.
rows.anchor: كل معدود متنقص وكل متوقع آت

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
rows.claim: A report glosses God's count comprehensively as everything, down to each breath.
rows.anchor: قال كل شيء حتى النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls this the most comprehensive report and treats the mention of breaths in other reports as an example.
rows.anchor: وهي أشمل الروايات ولا يبعد أن يستفاد منها أن ذكر النفس في الروايات من قبيل ذكر المثال

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The Godfearing will be gathered to the Merciful riding on mounts.
rows.anchor: وفدا } قال يحشرون على النجائب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Ali that a delegation arrives only mounted and that the Godfearing are people God loved, selected, and approved.
rows.anchor: يا علي الوفد لا يكون إلا ركبانا أولئك رجال اتقوا الله عز وجل فأحبهم وأختصهم ورضي أعمالهم فسماهم الله متقين

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: A further long report describes the Godfearing leaving their graves, riding the camels of Paradise, entering Paradise, and enjoying its blessings.
rows.anchor: روى القمي حديثا آخر طويلا يذكر صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فيه تفصيل خروجهم من قبورهم وركوبهم من نوق الجنة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Godfearing are brought on unmatched Paradise camels with gold saddles and emerald reins; they ride until they reach Paradise's gate.
rows.anchor: أما والله ما يحشرون على أقدامهم ولا يساقون سوقا ولكنهم يؤتون بنوق من الجنة لم تنظر الخلائق إلى مثلها

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The covenant with the Merciful is allegiance to the authority of Ali and the Imams after him.
rows.anchor: إلا من دان بولاية أمير المؤمنين والأئمة من بعده فهو العهد عند الله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says that bringing joy to a believer pleases the Prophet, and pleasing him constitutes a covenant with God.
rows.anchor: من أدخل على مؤمن سرورا فقد سرني ومن سرني فقد اتخذ عند الله عهدا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report identifies keeping the covenant with guarding the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: أن المحافظة على العهد هو المحافظة على الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i synthesizes the reports as diverse instances of the covenant: true belief or a righteous deed that saves a believer at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يستفاد من مجموعها أن العهد المأخوذ عند الله اعتقاد حق أو عمل صالح ينجي المؤمن يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited reports fit the verse only if those who possess intercession includes its recipients, or both intercessors and recipients; they do not address intercessors alone.
rows.anchor: ممن يملك الشفاعة في الآية هو الذي ينال الشفاعة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The report identifies the claim that God has a son and that angels are female as the claim being answered in these verses.
rows.anchor: هذا حيث قالت قريش إن لله عز وجل ولدا وأن الملائكة إناث

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The expression “a dreadful thing” means a tremendous claim; the heavens nearly split, the earth cleaves, and mountains collapse because of it.
rows.anchor: يعني مما قالوه ومما رموه به

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Every being in heaven and earth comes to the Merciful as a servant, having been counted individually, and comes alone on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The love God promises believers is the authority and allegiance of Ali.
rows.anchor: قال ولاية أمير المؤمنين هي الود الذي ذكره الله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet asks Ali to pray for a covenant and affection among believers; the verse then descends concerning Ali.
rows.anchor: اللهم اجعل لي عندك عهدا واجعل لي عندك ودا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Ali and glosses its promised love as love in believers' hearts.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال نزلت في علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One reported view makes the verse specific to Ali, whom every believer loves.
rows.anchor: قيل فيه أقوال أحدها أنها خاصة في علي فما من مؤمن إلا وفي قلبه محبة لعلي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir reports that the Prophet asked Ali to pray for a covenant and love in believers' hearts, after which this verse was revealed; a similar report is attributed to Jabir.
rows.anchor: حدثني أبو جعفر الباقر عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Al-Alusi infers that the verse is Medinan if this reported occasion is accepted.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الآية على هذا مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says none of the reports establishes that Ali's prayer occurred in Medina.
rows.anchor: وأنت خبير بأن لا دلالة في شيء من الأحاديث على وقوع القصة في المدينة أصلا

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
rows.claim: A report says that after migrating to Medina, Abd al-Rahman grieved leaving several companions in Mecca, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أنه لما هاجر إلى المدينة وجد في نفسه على فراق أصحابه بمكة منهم شيبة بن ربيعة وعتبة بن ربيعة وأميه بن خلف فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects this as a Medinan occasion because the whole sura is unanimously considered Meccan.
rows.anchor: صريح الحديث كون الآية مدنية ويدفعه اتفاق الكل على كون السورة بجميع آياتها مكية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Ali that the promised love is affection in the hearts of believers and the angels nearest to God, alongside other gifts bestowed on believers.
rows.anchor: المحبة في قلوب المؤمنين والملائكة المقربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i glosses “miqqah” as love and says other Sunni reports based on the verse's general wording do not conflict with a specific occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: أقول المقة المحبة وفي معناه بعض روايات أخر من طرق أهل السنة مبنية على عموم لفظ الآية وهو لا ينافي خصوص مورد النزول

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify the appointed term with Resurrection; al-Tabataba'i rejects this for lack of evidence.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن المراد بالأجل المسمى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others identify the appointed term with the prior divine word, making the two expressions explanatory apposition; al-Tabataba'i also rejects this for lack of evidence.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون إن الأجل المسمى هو الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior divine word decrees a delay, while the appointed term fixes its time; together they are the complete reason punishment is postponed, rather than independent causes.
rows.anchor: لولا أن الكلمة التي سبقت من ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing God as the Prophet's Lord honors and supports the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي إضافة الرب إلى ضمير الخطاب إعزاز وتأييد للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God delays punishment for what people say, the Prophet should patiently accept God's decree, reject their shirk, and praise God for the effects of that decree.
rows.anchor: إذا كان من قضاء الله أن يؤخر عذابهم ولا يعاجلهم بالانتقام على ما يقولون فلا يبقى لك إلا أن تصبر راضيا على ما قضاه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorification rejects attributing evil to God, while praise recognizes that events permitted by Him are beautiful in their wider benefits and ordering of the world.
rows.anchor: لها نسبة إلى فواعلها وليست إلا سيئة يجب تنزيهه تعالى عنها ولها نسبة بالإذن إليه تعالى وهي بهذه النسبة جميلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrases before sunrise and before sunset are temporal modifiers of the command to glorify God.
rows.anchor: ظرفان متعلقان بقوله { وسبح بحمد ربك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Some of the night times” uses a partitive min; anāʾ is the plural of inā or inw, meaning a time, and the phrase specifies when to glorify.
rows.anchor: والآناء على أفعال جمع إني أو إنو بكسر الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted phrase “and Me alone fear” in 2:40 has a comparable construction.
rows.anchor: الجملة نظيرة قوله وإياي فارهبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The edges of the day” is accusative after an omitted preposition and coordinated with the phrase about night; its implied sense is glorify during the day's edges.
rows.anchor: منصوب بنزع الخافض على ما ذكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not lexically require obligatory prayers; some exegetes read general glorification, while most follow early authorities such as Qatada in identifying prayer.
rows.anchor: وما ذكر في الآية من التسبيح مطلق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The prayer interpretation maps before sunrise to dawn, before sunset to afternoon, night times to sunset and night prayers, and day edges to noon.
rows.anchor: وقوله { ومن آناء الليل } صلاتا المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: To make noon fall at the day’s edges, interpreters divide daytime into halves and treat noon as a boundary of both halves.
rows.anchor: لو نصف النهار حصل نصفان الأول والأخير وصلاة الظهر في الجزء الأول من النصف الثاني فهي في طرف النصف الأول

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The plural “edges” is explained either as a plural used for two or by taking day generically, with two edges for every day.
rows.anchor: الأشهر الأعرف كون أقل الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls the explanations that make midday an edge strained and contrary to ordinary understanding and conversational usage.
rows.anchor: يأبى أن يسمي وسط النهار أطراف النهار

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A broader reading takes glorification as inward remembrance, spoken praise, or both, and identifies the times as dawn, afternoon, and night.
rows.anchor: وأما من قال إن المراد بالتسبيح والتحميد غير الفرائض من مطلق التسبيح والحمد إما بتذكر تنزيهه والثناء عليه تعالى قلبا وإما بقول مثل سبحان الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: On the general-remembrance reading, dawn and afternoon are repeated at the day edges; some accept repetition for emphasis, while others include midday too.
rows.anchor: وأما لزوم التكرار بذكر تسبيح الصبح والعصر مرتين فقد التزم به بعضهم قائلا أن ذلك للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative general-remembrance reading faces the same problem of explaining “edges,” since neither dawn and afternoon nor midday naturally matches the plural phrase.
rows.anchor: والإشكال كله ناش من ناحية قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i proposes that “the edges of the day” is a comitative object, with the time preposition implicit, and refers to the broad intervals before sunrise and sunset.
rows.anchor: قوله { وأطراف النهار } مفعول معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those broad intervals contain multiple parts, each an edge relative to midday, just as the early and late portions of a day can be expressed in both singular and plural.
rows.anchor: بالنظر إلى كونهما وقتين ذوي سعة لكل منهما أجزاء كل جزء منها طرف بالنسبة إلى وسط النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time relation is implicit on both sides: night is introduced by partitive min, while “day edges” likewise means alongside the times when glorification occurs.
rows.anchor: وهو مدخول من ولا معنى لتقدير في معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the non-prayer reading, the command covers parts of the day's beginning, end, and night without repeated times or a plural-used-for-two problem.
rows.anchor: كان المراد التسبيح في أجزاء من أول النهار وأجزاء من آخره وأجزاء من الليل بمعية أجزاء أول النهار وآخره ولم يلزم محذور التكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the prayer reading, the verse commands dawn, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers, but not noon; Hud 11:114 gives a similar four-prayer pattern.
rows.anchor: وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the suras of Ta-Ha and Hud preceded the post-Ascension al-Isra, the daily prayers may then have been four; five were later instituted, as in 17:78.
rows.anchor: الفرائض اليومية إنما شرعت خمسا في المعراج كما ذكرت في سورة الإسراء النازلة بعد المعراج خمسا في قوله أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, “so that you may be satisfied” means becoming content with God's decree, much like the instruction to seek help through patience and prayer.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فاصبر وسبح بحمد ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persistent glorification and praise deepen familiarity with God and awareness of the beauty of His acts, quieting distractions and producing contentment in the soul.
rows.anchor: إدامة ذكره بالتسبيح والتحميد تورث الرضا بقضائه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Other interpretations say the satisfaction is through intercession and a high rank with God, or through all promises of victory, religious honor, intercession, and Paradise.
rows.anchor: الشفاعة والدرجة الرفيعة عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not extend your eyes” means do not fix one's gaze on something; extending the gaze is a metonym for attachment to and love of it.
rows.anchor: مد العين مد نظرها وإطالته ففيه مجاز عقلي ثم مد النظر وإطالته إلى شيء كناية عن التعلق به وحبه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: “Groups among them” may mean classes of unbelievers or their male and female pairings and households; the indefinite plural minimizes their importance.
rows.anchor: الأصناف من الكفار أو الأزواج من النساء والرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The flower of worldly life” explains what God has granted them: its adornment and brightness; their enjoyment is a test, with some interpreting it as punishment through wealth and children.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة التفسير لقوله { ما متعنا به }

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi reports that the Prophet sought flour on credit for a guest and offered his armor as security; the verse was said to console him about worldly life.
rows.anchor: أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ضيفا ولم يكن عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ما يصلحه فأرسلني إلى رجل من اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the proposed occasion involving a loan and the Prophet's armor because the verse, especially its conclusion, does not fit that story.
rows.anchor: ومضمون الآية وخاصة ذيلها لا يلائم القصة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report says that after the command to pray, the Prophet came to Ali's doorway for eight months, urging prayer and reciting the purification verse; another version says nine months.
rows.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يجيء إلى باب علي

rows.speaker: أبو الحميراء
rows.claim: Abu al-Hamra says he witnessed the Prophet visit Ali and Fatima's door for forty mornings, greet the Household, and urge prayer.
rows.anchor: شهدت النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أربعين صباحا يجيء إلى باب علي وفاطمة فيأخذ بعضادتي الباب ثم يقول السلام عليكم أهل البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says reports giving nine months reflect the witness's observation rather than a fixed duration; their apparent Medinan setting is difficult for a Meccan verse, though one report describes visits in Medina.
rows.anchor: التقييد بتسعة أشهر مبني على ما شاهده الراوي لا على تحديد أصل إتيانه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
rows.claim: When hardship or poverty struck his household, the Prophet told them to pray and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: إذا نزلت بأهله شدة أو ضيق أمرهم بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that the Prophet directed his family to pray during hardship, including reports from Thabit, show that the verse's glorification can be understood broadly to include prayer.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على التوسع في معنى التسبيح في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the reading that God misguides whoever follows Satan; scripture instead says God gives Satan power over those who follow him, and the alternative also disrupts the pronoun's antecedent.
rows.anchor: لا شاهد من كلامه تعالى على هذه الكتابة المدعاة وإنما المذكور في كلامه تعالى القضاء بتسليط إبليس على من تولاه واتبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms knowledge, guidance, and an illuminating book may denote rational proof, inward divine guidance for sincere worshippers, and revelation, though the mapping between knowledge and guidance may be reversed.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يكون المراد بالعلم ما تفيده الحجة العقلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These three routes to knowledge are reason, inward insight, and hearing revelation, as also indicated by the command not to follow what one lacks knowledge of.
rows.anchor: وتلك طرق ثلاث إلى مطلق العلم العقل والبصر والسمع وقد أشار تعالى إليها في قوله ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Bending his side” combines bending with the side and idiomatically depicts turning away in arrogance.
rows.anchor: الثني الكسر والعطف بكسر العين الجانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal phrase means that the ignorant, arrogant disputant argues about God in order to mislead people; such figures are the followed leaders among the polytheists.
rows.anchor: واللام للتعليل أي يجادل في الله بجهل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat promises humiliation and disgrace in worldly life, followed by the punishment of burning in the hereafter; Mecca's chiefs met the worldly disgrace.
rows.anchor: وهو الهوان والذلة والفضيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment answers what the person's hands sent, whether the prefixed bi means recompense or cause; the shift from third to second person directly records blame.
rows.anchor: للمقابلة كقولنا بعت هذا بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God is not unjust to servants” is coordinated with their deeds: God does not wrong them but treats each according to what their deeds merit.
rows.anchor: أي ذلك لأن الله لا يظلم عباده بل يعامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping God “on an edge” describes a wavering person who bases worship on favorable circumstances alone and uses religion for worldly gain.
rows.anchor: وهذا صنف آخر من الناس غير المؤمنين الصالحين وهو الذي يعبد الله سبحانه بانيا عبادته على جانب واحد دون كل جانب وعلى تقدير لا على كل تقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When hardship comes, such a worshipper turns back, either pessimistic about religion or hoping to escape the ordeal; like idolaters, he loses worldly security and the hereafter through apostasy.
rows.anchor: فهذا المذبذب المنقلب على وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The edge is a metaphor for worship conditional on one side of experience; the following clauses explain it, with worldly loss through hardship and afterlife loss through turning away.
rows.anchor: وعليه فقوله { يعبد الله على حرف } من قبيل الاستعارة بالكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An idol cannot harm or benefit because it lacks awareness and will; the harm and loss its worshipper suffers comes from the worshipper's own act.
rows.anchor: فإنه لفقده الشعور والإرادة لا يتوجه منه إلى عابده نفع أو ضرر والذي يصيب عابده من ضرر وخسران فإنما يصيبه من ناحية العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about calling one whose harm is nearer than benefit, “calls” means “says”; the relative phrase is the subject, and the following curse is the answer to an omitted oath.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ دخلت عليه لام الابتداء وهو موصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idol-worshipper will call his supposed protector a wretched patron and companion after seeing that its worship brought eternal punishment and ruin.
rows.anchor: وإنما يعد ضره أقرب من نفعه لما يشاهد يوم القيامة ما تستتبعه عبادته له من العذاب الخالد والهلاك المؤبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers who do good are contrasted with three classes of disbelievers: arrogant leaders, imitators who follow rebellious devils, and wavering worshippers; this prepares for judgment between them.
rows.anchor: ووصفهم بالضلال والخسران قابلهم بهذا الصنف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report describes angels recording what is decreed for a fetus from a tablet that reaches its mother's forehead, while stipulating possible change in what they write.
rows.anchor: الملكين يكتبان جميع ما قدر له عن لوح يقرع جبهة أمه فيكتبان جميع ما في اللوح ويشترطان البداء فيما يكتبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports are reconciled by two tablets: the Preserved Tablet cannot change, while the Tablet of Effacement and Confirmation can; decree accordingly has inevitable and non-inevitable forms.
rows.anchor: فإن لكل شيء ومنها الإنسان نصيبا في اللوح المحفوظ الذي لا سبيل للتغير والتبدل إلى ما كتب فيه ونصيبا من لوح المحو والإثبات الذي يقبل التغير والتبدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete causal chains do not change, incomplete chains can; inevitability in decree does not negate the voluntary character of human acts.
rows.anchor: سلسلة العلل التامة ومعلولاتها ولا تقبل تغييرا وسلسلة العلل الناقصة مع معاليلها وهي القابلة وكأن الصنف الأول من الروايات يشير إلى ما يقضى للجنين من قضاء محتوم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: “Formed” refers to particles created in Adam's loins under the covenant and carried through later generations; “unformed” includes expelled semen and miscarried fetuses before ensoulment.
rows.anchor: قال المخلقة هم الذر الذين خلقهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation of this report was explained earlier in the discussion of the primordial covenant.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم توضيح معنى الحديث في البحث الروائي المتعلق بآية الذر في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report attributed to al-Sadiq through his father says that reaching one hundred years is the most decrepit stage of life.
rows.anchor: قال إذا بلغ العبد مائة سنة فذلك أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Bedouins who accepted Islam stayed with it after good harvests, rain, and healthy births but abandoned it after drought or bad outcomes for their children.
rows.anchor: كان ناس من الأعراب يأتون النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فيسلمون فإذا رجعوا إلى بلادهم فإن وجدوا عام غيث وعام خصب وعام ولاد حسن قالوا إن ديننا هذا صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i cites this as a report of the verse's occasion and notes that he discussed the hundred-year tradition under 16:70.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم بعض الروايات في هذا المعنى في تفسير سورة النحل في ذيل الآية 70

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The same account of Bedouins judging Islam by favorable or adverse worldly outcomes is also reported through another route.
rows.anchor: أقول وهذا المعنى مروي عنه أيضا بغير هذا الطريق

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Another report describes people who affirmed one God but doubted Muhammad's prophethood, deciding whether to believe him based on wealth and health for themselves and their children.
rows.anchor: قوم وحدوا الله وخلعوا عبادة من يعبد من دون الله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: In this report, worldly “good” means health, a trial means personal affliction, and turning back means shifting from doubt to polytheism and worshipping idols.
rows.anchor: يعني بلاء في نفسه { انقلب على وجهه } انقلب على شكه إلى الشرك

rows.speaker: الصدوق
rows.claim: Al-Saduq transmits the same report in al-Tawhid with slight variation.
rows.anchor: ورواه الصدوق في التوحيد باختلاف يسير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One who thinks God will not help Muhammad can tie a rope to his roof and hang himself; the author treats this as Ibn Abbas's exegesis functioning like an occasion report.
rows.anchor: قال فليربط حبلا { إلى السماء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i includes the report because, despite being Ibn Abbas's interpretation, it conveys the verse's occasion.
rows.anchor: هو وإن كان تفسيرا منه لكنه في معنى سبب النزول ولذلك أوردناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Behind them” means ahead and surrounding them: the future is said to be behind a person because it approaches and overtakes him.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكونه وراءهم كونه أمامهم محيطا بهم وسمي وراءهم بعناية أنه يطلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barzakh is the grave realm, an imaginal life after death until Resurrection, supported by the context, other verses, and abundant Shiite and Sunni reports.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهذا البرزخ عالم القبر وهو عالم المثال الذي يعيش فيه الإنسان بعد موته إلى قيام الساعة على ما يعطيه السياق وتدل عليه آيات أخر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the barrier merely prevents return to worldly life until Resurrection; al-Tabataba'i rejects this because the context places the barrier between death and Resurrection and the time limit would be pointless.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالآية أن بينهم وبين الدنيا حاجزا يمنعهم من الرجوع إليها إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The trumpet is the second blast that revives the dead, not the first blast that kills the living, because the listed consequences belong to the resurrection.
rows.anchor: المراد به النفخة الثانية التي تحيا فيها الأموات دون النفخة الأولى التي تموت فيها الأحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of family ties negates their worldly effects: kinship matters for household and social cooperation, which has no place in the accounting and recompense of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: نفي لآثار الأنساب بنفي أصلها فإن الذي يستوجب حفظ الأنساب واعتبارها هي الحوائج الدنيوية التي تدعو الإنسان إلى الحياة الاجتماعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Nor ask one another” names the clearest effect of kinship, asking relatives about each other to seek help and avert harm; this concerns the reckoning, not later inhabitants of Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: وقوله { ولا يتساءلون } ذكر لأظهر آثار الأنساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Scales” may be plural of balance or of weighed deeds; their weight and lightness were discussed under al-A'raf.
rows.anchor: الموازين جمع الميزان أو جمع الموزون وهو العمل

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Lafh and nafh both describe heat striking the face, but lafh is stronger, like a scorching poisonous blast; nafh is a breeze touching the face.
rows.anchor: إلا أن اللفح أشد تأثيرا وأعظم من النفح

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Kuluḥ is the lips contracting away from the teeth until the teeth show.
rows.anchor: والكلوح تقلص الشفتين عن الأسنان حتى تبدو الأسنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire makes the lips contract and the teeth show, leaving faces like roasted heads.
rows.anchor: يصيب وجوههم لهب النار حتى تتقلص شفاههم وتنكشف عن أسنانهم كالرؤوس المشوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about God's signs means they will be asked whether the signs were recited to them and they denied them.
rows.anchor: أي يقال لهم ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم بها تكذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wretchedness is the opposite of happiness; a person's allotted good is lost in wretchedness, or wretchedness is the evil that characterizes them.
rows.anchor: وعادة الشيء ما يختص به من الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wording that misery overcame them hints that they acquired it through bad choices; their promise to act well if returned confirms that their state relates to voluntary action.
rows.anchor: وفي إضافة الشقوة إلى أنفسهم تلويح إلى أن لهم صنعا في شقوتهم من جهة اكتسابهم ذلك بسوء اختيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They imagine themselves as neutral beings overcome by misery, but their misery is their own through bad choices and deeds; this is an admission that the proof against them was complete.
rows.anchor: الشقوة شقوة أنفسهم أي شقوة لازمة لسوء اختيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their confession and denial on Judgment Day merely express settled dispositions: some lie and deny the truth despite seeing it.
rows.anchor: كما أنهم يكذبون يومئذ وينكرون أشياء مع ظهور الحق ومعاينته لاستقرار ملكة الكذب والإنكار في نفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request to be brought back to worldly life seeks the cause by naming its result: they want to repent, do righteous deeds, and attain happiness.
rows.anchor: سؤال منهم للرجوع إلى الدنيا على ما تدل عليه آيات أخر فهو من قبيل طلب المسبب بطلب سببه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib glosses “be gone” as contemptuously driving off a dog; here it figuratively means rebuking them, sending them away, and silencing them.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب خسأت الكلب فخسأ أي زجرته مستهينا به فانزجر وذلك إذا قلت له اخسأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers in the verse are worldly believers whose faith was repentance; their prayer for mercy asks for success in doing good and entering Paradise.
rows.anchor: سؤالا منهم أن يوفقهم للسعادة فيعملوا صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' prayer and the damned's plea have the same basic meaning—repentance and a request for felicity—but differ because one is in the world of action and the other in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فكان ما قاله المؤمنون في الدنيا معناه التوبة وسؤال الفوز بالسعادة وذلك عين ما قاله هؤلاء مما معناه التوبة وسؤال الفوز بالسعادة وإنما الفرق بينهما من حيث الموقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address is to unbelievers and the absent pronouns refer to believers; “My remembrance” means the believers' prayer, which mockery kept the unbelievers from remembering.
rows.anchor: وهو معنى قول الكفار في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards believers on the day of requital for patiently remembering Him while mocked; the exclusivity clause means they, rather than the mockers, are the winners.
rows.anchor: ومتعلق الصبر معلوم من السياق محذوف للإيجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These four verses end the unbelievers' hope: confession and repentance benefit in worldly life, which believers used but mockers abandoned; on the day of recompense they cannot perform new deeds.
rows.anchor: إياس قطعي للكفار من الفوز بسبب ما تعلقوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about years spent on earth concerns the time in graves, not simply worldly life; a proposal to include both worldly life and barzakh is also mentioned.
rows.anchor: ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون ما لبثوا غير ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer that they stayed a day or part of one earthly day because, beside eternal life now visible to them, their grave stay seems brief; other verses estimate an hour or part of a day.
rows.anchor: وقد استقلوا اللبث في الأرض حينما قايسوه بالبقاء الأبدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ask the counters” means they cannot count the duration accurately and should ask those who counted; these may be the angels who count the days.
rows.anchor: أي نحن لا نحسن إحصاءها فاسأل الذين يعدونه وفسر بالملائكة العادين للأيام وليس ببعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God confirms that their grave stay was brief and wishes they had known in worldly life that they would soon be raised, instead of denying Resurrection and facing endless punishment.
rows.anchor: المعنى قال الله الأمر كما قلتم فما مكثتم إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects treating “if only you knew” as a conditional with an omitted consequence, and finds a concessive reading even less plausible because it lacks a coordinating waw.
rows.anchor: بعضهم " لو " في الآية شرطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing death, the grave, resurrection, judgment, and recompense, God rebukes those who thought they were created without lasting purpose or a return to Him.
rows.anchor: بعد ما بين ما سيستقبلهم من أحوال الموت ثم اللبث في البرزخ ثم البعث بما فيه من الحساب والجزاء وبخهم على حسبانهم أنهم لا يبعثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's kingship gives Him authority over creation and return; because He is true, His decrees are true, and because no other deity exists, He alone rules the cosmic throne and its commands.
rows.anchor: فله أن يحكم بما شاء من بدء وعود

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Qummi reports from al-Sadiq that barzakh is an intermediate state of reward and punishment between worldly life and the hereafter, and that the Imam fears for people concerning barzakh.
rows.anchor: قال البرزخ هو أمر بين أمرين وهو الثواب والعقاب بين الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Sajjad says a grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of Fire.
rows.anchor: إن القبر إما روضة من رياض الجنة أو حفرة من حفر النار

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq rejects the claim that believers' spirits are inside green birds around the Throne: believers are too honored for this and dwell in bodies like their own.
rows.anchor: المؤمن أكرم على الله من أن يجعل روحه في حوصلة طير

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: One report says believers' spirits dwell in a tree in Paradise, eating and drinking while asking God to hasten the Hour and join later believers with earlier ones.
rows.anchor: إن أرواح المؤمنين لفي شجرة من الجنة يأكلون من طعامها ويشربون من شرابها ويقولون ربنا أقم الساعة لنا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Another report places spirits in body-like forms in a Paradise tree, where they recognize one another and ask about those still living or dead.
rows.anchor: إن الأرواح في صفة الأجساد في شجرة في الجنة تتعارف وتتسأل فإذا قدمت الروح على الأرواح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports detailing barzakh and the conditions of believers and others there are numerous and mutawatir, with some already discussed in earlier sections.
rows.anchor: أقول أخبار البرزخ وتفاصيل ما يجري على المؤمنين وغيرهم فيه كثيرة متواترة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says every lineage and kinship is cut off on Judgment Day except the Prophet's lineage and family connection.
rows.anchor: كل حسب ونسب منقطع يوم القيامة إلا حسبي ونسبي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Other reports preserve the exception with varying wording: the Prophet's lineage, relation, and in-law ties remain.
rows.anchor: كل سبب ونسب منقطع يوم القيامة إلا سببي ونسبي

rows.speaker: زين العابدين
rows.claim: Al-Sajjad says Paradise is for obedient people regardless of ancestry and Fire for disobedient people regardless of Qurayshi descent; only righteous deeds sent ahead will help.
rows.anchor: خلق الله الجنة لمن أطاع وأحسن ولو كان عبدا حبشيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's context resists limiting its general denial of kinship; a possible benefit of the Prophet's lineage is that his descendants are enabled to do good deeds that help them.
rows.anchor: سياق الآية كالآبي عن التخصيص ولعل من آثار نسبه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يوفق ذريته من صالح العمل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Qummi explains that the fire blazes over and burns their faces, while their grimacing means open mouths and darkened faces.
rows.anchor: قال تلهب عليهم فتحرقهم { وهم فيها كالحون }

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq explains that their own deeds made them wretched.
rows.anchor: عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا } قال بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Ja'far rejects the claim that people were created for extinction: they were created to abide and move from one abode to another, since Paradise does not perish and Fire does not go out.
rows.anchor: خلقنا للبقاء وكيف تفنى جنة لا تبيد

rows.speaker: الملائكة
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses “ask the counters” as asking angels who count days and record the hours and deeds people acquire.
rows.anchor: الملائكة الذين يعدون علينا الأيام

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says God asks the saved and damned how long they lived; their answer of a day or part of one becomes a contrast between a good trade for mercy and a bad trade for punishment.
rows.anchor: إن الله إذا أدخل أهل الجنة الجنة وأهل النار النار قال لأهل الجنة كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the report's fit with the verse's context and parallel passages is unclear, and refers back to his earlier interpretation.
rows.anchor: وفي انطباق معنى الحديث على الآية بما لها من السياق وبما يشهد به الآيات النظائر خفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contrasts believers, whose good works guide them to God's knowledge and lasting reward, with unbelievers whose works lead only to mirage and layered darkness.
rows.anchor: تميز المؤمنين منهم بأن المؤمنين مهديون بأعمالهم الصالحة إلى نور من ربهم يفيدهم معرفة الله سبحانه ويسلك بهم إلى أحسن الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is universal light: His self-manifestation brings the heavens and earth into existence, unlike sensory light, which reveals already existing bodies.
rows.anchor: ظهور الأشياء بالنور الإلهي عين وجودها وظهور الأجسام الكثيفة بالأنوار الحسية غير أصل وجودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The special light of knowledge grows from good deeds and will illuminate believers' hearts and sight at Resurrection, when they see openly what was hidden in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ونورا خاصا يستنير به المؤمنون ويهتدون إليه بأعمالهم الصالحة وهو نور المعرفة الذي سيستنير به قلوبهم وأبصارهم يوم تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light is represented by a lamp in a niche, clear glass like a shining star, and exceptionally pure oil, producing light upon light in houses of worship.
rows.anchor: ومثل تعالى هذا النور بمصباح في زجاجة في مشكاة يشتعل من زيت في نهاية الصفاء فتتلألأ الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري فتزيد نورا على نور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain, hail, alternating night and day, and creatures moving on their bellies, two legs, or four show God's unrestricted sovereignty over creation.
rows.anchor: يحكم بما أراد ينزل الودق والبرد من سحاب واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses connect with the preceding laws, which end by calling the revealed signs clear and admonitory; explaining truths is itself divine illumination, and the Qur'an is called light elsewhere.
rows.anchor: والآيات غير فاقدة للاتصال بما قبلها
